# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 57 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 57 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_057_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 5, Part 3 — The Son and the Holy Spirit

**57:1** "Lord," I said, "I still do not understand something. What is the son in the parable, and who is the flesh?" "Listen," he said. "The son is the Holy Spirit, and the flesh is the son of God."

**57:2** "How, lord," I said, "can the son of God be a slave?" "Listen," he said. "God planted the vineyard, that is, he created the people, and gave them to his son. And the son appointed the angels over them to guard them. And the son himself went through great suffering to cleanse them of their sins."

**57:3** "But the vineyard cleansed of weeds and beautified by digging — what is the cleansing of the vineyard?" "The weeds pulled out of the vineyard," he said, "are the iniquities of the servants of God; and the digging and the cleansing are the sufferings which the son of God suffered for the sake of the people. For the son of God bore their sins in order to cleanse them of their iniquities."

**57:4** "Why then, lord," I said, "did the son of God take on the form of the slave in this parable?" "Listen," he said. "The son of God did not come in the form of a grand personage, but in the form of a servant, that is, he was humbled."

---

*EMET renders the Greek of P.Mich. 130 with maximal literalness, preserving the Son/Holy Spirit christological discussion in Similitude 5.*
